newsitem.title: BULGARIA: BULGARIAN PREMIER BRACES FOR IMF FUNDING TALKS.
newsitem.headline: BULGARIAN PREMIER BRACES FOR IMF FUNDING TALKS.

text.p: Bulgaria's failure to meet macroeconomic targets may clog funding talks with the International Monetary Fund (IMF) this week, Prime Minister Zhan Videnov told a news conference on Tuesday.
"We will try to convince the IMF mission that all planned measures aimed at improving financial discipline...in the country have been fulfilled," Videnov said.

An IMF mission is due in Sofia on Wednesday to evaluate the country's reform performance, agree on reform policies that would release a crucial second $115 million loan and draft next year's budget frame.
"But the Fund will be interested mainly in the macroeconomic situation in the country, which unfortunately cannot be seen as favourable," said Videnov.
Bulgaria's gross domestic product (GDP) is expected to fall by between 8.1 percent and 10.5 percent this year and by 2.0 to 4.0 percent in 1997, the National Statistics Institute said.

The government's budget revision made in July forecast zero GDP growth this year, down from an originally planned three percent, annual consumer price inflation of 100 percent and an average annual central interest rate of 68 percent.
However, huge domestic debt burdens and a banking crisis had pushed the annual interest rate to an all-time high of 300 percent last month, which was cut to 240 percent 10 days ago.
The IMF postponed a $115 million tranche last month until the government fulfilled its pledges to close down loss-making state enterprises and speed up privatisation.
"The biggest loss-makers have been liquidated," said Videnov.
Two or three state loss-making companies out of the pledged 64 have not yet been closed due to legal problems, he added.
"Liquidation of banks which proved to be an endless source of squandering of public and financial resources is under way," he added.

The Bulgarian National Bank (BNB) has placed 14 banks in receivership in a bid to stabilise the crumbling financial system. The BNB has sought bankruptcy for five of them through the courts, which so far have delayed ruling.
Unwise lending has sunk many local banks and produced many so called credit millionaires.
Videnov said Bulgaria's mass privatisation programme is on track and legislation for cash privatisation is in place to attract future foreign investors. -- Sofia Newsroom, 359-2-84561
